```text
     If you don’t have a competitive edge, don’t compete.
                                                               Jack Welch

   While Jack Welch was almost certainly talking about business and not
games in the above quote, I think it applies equally to poker. A competi-
tive advantage is anything that tips the odds of success in your favor.
Obtaining a high level of poker strategy can certainly tip the odds in your
favor, but there is another level of competitive advantage that you can
add to your arsenal and that’s a mindset advantage. I wrote this book with
one goal in mind: to teach you the psychological tactics and strategies
that will show you how to perform at the outer limits of your capabilities
more consistently.
   Since I wrote Positive Poker I have provided peak performance consult-
ing to hundreds of poker players, hosted dozens of podcasts with Elliot Roe
on the podcast The Mindset Advantage, and witnessed an explosion of re-
search within the fields of neuroscience and peak performance psychology.
To say that psychology is a dynamic field is quite an understatement. New
```

```text
Peak Poker Performance

unearthed. This book is a culmination of all the work I’ve been doing over
the last few years.
    It covers information on how super successful poker players think and
it’s about the actions they take regularly to ensure peak poker perform-
ance (or at the very least to increase the probability of playing at the peak
of their capabilities). True success starts with a state of mind. How you
think is almost as important as what you think. Besides that, it takes spe-
cific actions and behaviors to move from intentions to actions. The differ-
ence between being a winner and being a loser has at least as much to do
with mental attitude as it does with skill development. This book was
written to show you how you can enhance your mind to achieve your full
potential.
    Before we get into what it takes to achieve peak performance, let’s
consider some of the philosophical reasons why it is critical to seek out
peak performance. The great American humanist psychologist Abraham
Maslow theorized that we all have an inherent need to become all that we
can be. He wrote that our potential is clamoring to be used. Basically, if
there is a gap between your ideal self (how you would like to be) and your
real self (how you actually are), angst, anxiety, and regret are likely to re-
sult. The way to alleviate these negative states is via the choices you
make. You see, Maslow said that every moment of the day we have a
choice to make. We can either choose to step forward into growth or we
can step back into the safety of our comfort zone. This book was de-
signed to help you bridge the gap between where you are now and where
you would like to be. If you want to get out of your comfort zone and un-
derstand yourself better, you have come to the right place.
    It will provide you with concrete strategies that, if followed, will sig-
nificantly improve your mental game. The material covered includes spe-
cific, clinically proven techniques that will show you how to manage your
emotions, optimize your brain, build peak performance habits, and train
your mindset for better results. If you want to stretch yourself so that
you become a great poker player and if you are committed to the proc-
ess, you can reach greatness.
```

```text
                                                                Introduction

  Here is a summary of the core peak performance principles that are
covered in the upcoming chapters.

Principle 1: Have a Compelling Vision
Even the most motivated poker player can get caught up in daily drama
and stresses and forget “why” they became motivated to play poker in
the first place. A compelling vision can act as a catalyst for peak perform-
ance. Your “why” is what’s going to help you get from where you are now
to where you want to be. Knowing your why can:

   ♠ increase your motivation to succeed
   ♠ expand your thinking about what’s possible for you to achieve
   ♠ push you to continue when you feel like giving up
   ♠ give you energy to keep working or going.

   Besides knowing why you are committed to poker, it is also important
to think about what you would specifically like to achieve. There’s a prov-
erb attributed to Confucius that goes, “When you chase two rabbits, you
catch none.” This means that you need to have a clear focus or vision of
what peak performance looks like to you. What could you achieve, for in-
stance, in the next year that would make the year a huge success for
you? What is the most important thing for you to focus your attention on
each day? Work backward to figure out what needs to happen for you to
achieve your overall goals. Simplify your focus and identify what’s most
important and commit to accomplishing it every single day.

Principle 2: Create Winning Habits and Systems
It’s important to realize that just having a compelling vision is only the
starting point of the journey to success. As Grant Cardone says in his
book The 10X Rule, there are no shortcuts to success. The more action
you take, the more likely it is that you will get a break. He reiterates that
```
